values.note: Free, first come; no reservations at Kansas state fishing lakes. Seven consecutive days at a state fishing lake, then five days away (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), amended 2023); a longer stay needs a written KDWP permit.

booking.source: KDWP camping page (Wayback 2025-10-28): 'camping first-come, first served and reservations are not accepted', 'a stay of not more than seven consecutive days'; K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), Kansas Register 2023-04-06; the Jewell page posts no different limit. Read 2026-11-06

hookups.source: KDWP Jewell page (Wayback 2026-07-11) lists only picnic shelters, tables, grills, fire rings and two pit toilets - no hookups at the six designated sites; the KDWP camping page sets state fishing lakes apart from the state parks' serviced sites. Read 2026-11-06

facilities.source: KDWP Jewell page (Wayback 2026-07-11): 'two pit toilets', facility list 'Vault Toilet / Type of Facility: Pit Toilet'. Read 2026-11-06

note: KDWP state fishing lake in grassland hills between Glen Elder and Lovewell reservoirs. Camping only at six designated sites around the lake (Cattail Cove, Panfish Flats, Willow's Weep, Catfish Cove, Plum Thicket Shores, Ash Creek); Trappers Hollow, Turtlehead Bend and Limestone Point are day use only, and no camping at the reservable group shelter. Seven picnic shelters, five fishing piers, two pit toilets, fires in metal rings only. Boats at no wake, for fishing and hunting; no swimming. --Claude
summary: KDWP Jewell page (Wayback 2026-07-11): six named designated sites, free/FCFS, no hookups, two pit toilets; max 7 nights added (K.A.R.); vault_toilets added. Site locations aren't published, so waterfront and pin left as stored (lakeview/lakefront lead). Phone missing -> (785) 545-3345.
flags: WATERFRONT lead (apply.py doesn't write it): stored 'not waterfront' left alone, unconfirmed. KDWP names the six camping sites but gives no locations ('Google Earth Map' brochure https://www.ksoutdoors.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/350/638941405942600000 stayed unread: KDWP 403, Wayback 429). On Esri every developed gravel loop on this ~600 x 400 m lake sits at the shore: the north spur at the stored pin ends in a turnaround ~30-40 m from the water behind a narrow shrub band, with a gravel point running out into the lake; the east-shore loops (one beside the group shelter at ~39.6990,-98.2770 is on a bare point at the water) and the south-shore points by the dam are 5-30 m from open water. The names (Cove, Flats, Shores) suggest lakeside sites, so LAKEVIEW or LAKEFRONT is likely for most, but I can't tell which loops are camping and which are the three day-use areas, so I didn't move it up.

PIN 39.70094,-98.27986 is on grass beside the north spur's turnaround, ~40 m from the water; whether that loop is one of the six sites is not shown anywhere I could read. Not moved. Google's 39.69940,-98.27942 is in the lake.
PHONE missing (apply.py doesn't write it): propose (785) 545-3345, the Glen Elder Area Office listed as the contact on the Jewell page.
WEBSITE stored ksoutdoors.gov area page confirmed (live answers 403 to plain HTTP; Wayback copy current to 2026-07-11).
MAX STAY newly written 7 nights (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c)). Hookups re-sourced from the agency page (were derived from our note). vault_toilets true added.
NOTE: dropped 'Free, first-come, no hookups. Site lengths not published.' (fields hold it); added the day-use-only areas so a camper doesn't pull into one.
SITE SIZE / FIT: not published; the loops on imagery are wide gravel turnarounds on maintained gravel roads, which a 23-ft motorhome should manage.
SAND: none - gravel turnarounds on grass; no open-beach camping.
